MSE 1101.title: Introduction to Materials Science and Engineering
topics: History: Stone age to modern age, Examples of different types of materials, Classification of materials, Advanced materials.

Atomic Structure and Bonding: Fundamental concepts, Electrons in materials, Periodic table, Bonding forces and energies, Primary interatomic bonds, Secondary bonding, The structure of crystalline solids, Unit cells, Metallic crystal structure, Miller indices, Density computation, Crystallographic directions, Crystallographic planes, Introduction to X-ray diffraction.
Imperfection in solids: Point defects (vacancies, interstitials), Line defects (dislocations), Area defects (grain boundary defects), Dislocations and its interactions.

Mechanical Properties: Concepts of stress strain, True stress, True strain, Stress strain behavior, Elastic properties of materials, Elastic modulus, Deformation, Tensile strength and Yield strength, Elongation, Hardness, Ductile fracture, Brittle fracture, Toughness, High temperature properties and application, Creep, Fatigue.
Strengthening mechanism: Strengthening by grain size reduction, Solid-solution strengthening, Strain hardening, Precipitation hardening and other hardening techniques.

Composite: Dispersion-strengthened composites, Calculation of strength of composite materials, Polymer-matrix composites, Metal-matrix composites, Ceramic-matrix composites, Carbon-carbon composites, Processing of fiber-reinforced composites. Materials Properties: Electrical properties (electrical conductivity, electronic and ionic conduction, energy band structures in solids, electron mobility, electrical resistivity of metals, electrical characteristics of commercial alloys), Semiconductor, Superconductor magnetic properties, Optical properties, Aspects of materials in design.
Nondestructive testing: Introduction to basic principle of dye penetration testing, Magnetic particle testing, Ultrasound tests, Radiography and Eddy current testing.

DC Motors: Principle of operation, Speed equation, Classification, Characteristics of different types of DC motors, Starting of DC motors and methods for speed control.
Transformers: Working principle, Construction and Cooling, EMF equation, Equivalent circuits, Losses and efficiency.

Area under a plane curves in Cartesian and polar coordinates; Volume of solid revolution, Volume of hollow solids of revolutions by shell method; Area of surface of revolution.

MSE 3103.title: Materials Manufacturing Processes
topics: Ianufacturing Properties of Materials: Structure of matter; Metals and lloys; Deformation and mechanical properties of materials; Control of material roperties.

Foundry Practices: Properties of moulding sand; Sand additives; Pattern and mould making; Core and core boxes; Melting; Pouring; Gates and risers; Cooling and solidification; Chvorinov's rule; Solidification shrinkage; Riser design; Defects in casting; Miscellaneous casting processes; Inspection of casting; Non-ferrous casting metals; Cast iron.

Forming Processes: Introduction; Plastic deformation and yield criteria; Relationship between tensile and shear yield stresses; Mechanics of forming processes- rolling, forging, drawing, bending, extrusion; Various forming operations, Advantages and disadvantages of hot and cold forming; Friction and lubrication in metal forming; Defects in metal forming.

Machining Processes: Mechanics of basic machining operation; Machining processes- shaping and planning; Turning and boring; Drilling, Milling; Abrasive machining and finishing operation; Surface finish; Economics of machining operations.

Shaping Processes for Polymers, Ceramics and Glasses: Properties of polymer melts; extrusion; Defects in extrusion; Injection molding; Compression and transfer molding; Blow molding and rotational molding; Thermoforming, Processing of traditional and new ceramics; Shaping processes in glass working.
Powder Metallurgy: Principles of powder metallurgy process; Powder manufacture; Powder blending; Powder compaction; Sintering; Finishing.
Advanced Manufacturing Processes: Additive manufacturing; Laser processing and manufacturing.

MSE 3104.title: Materials Manufacturing Processes Sessional
topics: List of Experiments

Testing on foundry sand- Permeability for green sand, Compactability, Moisture determination, Sieve analysis and Grain fineness number, Wet and dry compression strength for green sand; Preparation of moulding sand mixtures; Melting and casting of ferrous and non-ferrous materials; Various casting processes; Structural analysis of cast metal; Hot working and cold working process; Metal working processes like Rolling, Forging, Extrusion, Wire, Rod and tube drawing, Sheet metal forming.

MSE 3105.title: Welding and Materials Joining Processes
topics: Materials Joining Methods: Introduction to permanent and semi-permanent methods of materials joining namely Welding, Brazing, Soldering, Riveting, Adhesives, Nuts and bolts and washers, Knock-down fittings, Screws.

Soldering and Brazing: Solders; Classifications of soldering fluxes and its properties; Different types of soldering methods; Basic operations of soldering: Cleaning operations; Types of brazing joint; Basic operations in brazing; Brazing filler metals; Brazing fluxes, Quality control in brazing, Brazing applications.

Fusion Welding Process: Classification of welding processes; Welding process selection criteria; Principle of fusion welding, Traditional fusion welding processes: Oxy Fuel welding, Manual metal arc welding, Gas metal arc welding, Gas tungsten arc welding; Modern fusion welding process: Submerged arc welding, Electro-slag welding, Plasma arc welding; Special fusion welding process: Electron beam welding, Laser beam welding; Thermite welding; Preparation of thermite welding.

Solid State Welding Process: Resistance welding processes; Resistance spot and seam welding process; Projection welding; Pressure welding, Cold and Hot pressure welding, Forge welding, Roll welding, Explosion welding, Friction welding and Diffusion bonding.

Metallurgical Aspects of Welding: Weld metal solidification and weld-pool structure; Heat affected Zone (HAZ); Effect of welding parameters and processes on HAZ; Weld metal nucleation mechanism; Grain structure control; Effect of welding parameters on grain structure; Oxidation and de-oxidation of metals in welding; Dissolution of gases and its control; Weldability; Develop, analyse and detect the remedies of residual stress and distortion fusion zone; Weld decay; Refining of weld metals.

Miscellaneous Joining Processes: Types of adhesives; Selection of adhesive materials; Post treatment of adhesive joined materials; Types of riveting; Selection criteria of rivet joining; Ceramics joining; Polymer joining process. Weld Defects: Weld metal solidification cracking; Reducing solidification cracking; Liquation cracking; Lamellar Tearing; Imperfect shape and unacceptable contour.

Weld Design and Symbols: Design of the weld; Reference line of welding symbol; Size of welds; Field weld and reference tail; Typical welding symbols. Inspection and Testing of Weldment: Inspection prior to welding; In-process inspection; Testing of weldments: metallographic test, chemical test, mechanical test; Non-Destructive testing (NDT).

MSE 3106.title: Welding and Materials Joining Processes Sessional
topics: This laboratory course will comprehensively help to understand various forms of welding/joining in addition to welding defects which affect mechanical properties of welded parts.
List of Experiments

Soldering Process (Lap Joint); Brazing Process (Lap Joint); Metal Cutting and Gas Welding (Butt Joint); Starting an Arc and Running Stringer (Straight) Beads; Manual Metal Arc Welding (MMAW) Process: Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW) and Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW); Micro and Macro Examination of a Welded Joint; Investigation of Mechanical Properties of Welded Joint; Determination of Shear Strength of Soldered, Brazed and Resistance Spot Welded Joints; Oxygen-Acetylene Welding (OAW).

MSE 3107.title: Physical Metallurgy of Materials
topics: Cold Working and Hot Working: Cold working, Effect of cold working on properties, Hot working, Recovery, Recrystallization, Nucleation and grain growth, Comparison of hot work and cold work.

Phase Transformation in Steel: Allotropic changes in iron, Iron-iron carbide equilibrium diagram, Cast iron, Steel and iron microstructures with phase relations, Transformation of steel on heating and cooling, Influence of alloying elements, Time-Temperature Transformation diagram, Continuous Cooling Transformation diagram, Effects of alloying elements on TTT diagram, Mechanism of pearlitic, Martensitic and bainitic transformation.

Heat Treatment Processes: Annealing, Normalizing, Hardening/Quenching, Hardenability: Jominy end-quench test, Mechanism of heat removal during quenching, Factors effecting quenching conditions, Tempering, Austempering and martempering process.

Surface Hardening and Surface Heat Treatment: Carburizing, Nitriding, Cyaniding, Flame hardening and Induction hardening, Laser and Electron beam hardening, Diffusion coating, Heat treatment of surface hardened materials.

Heat Treatment of Engineering Alloys: Heat treatment of cast iron-White cast iron, Grey cast iron, Heat treatment of non-ferrous alloys-Aluminum alloys, Copper alloys, Nickel alloys and Titanium alloys.
Application of Physical Metallurgy: Strengthening mechanisms of metals, Thermo mechanical treatment, Micro alloyed and ultra-high strength steel, Super alloy, Control of texture.

MSE 3108.title: Physical Metallurgy of Materials Sessional
topics: This laboratory course offers practical knowledge of macro- and micro-graphic studies of Heat-treated steel, Alloy steel, Tool steel, Case hardened steel and Cast iron.
List of Experiments

Annealing of pre-stressed sample, Normalising of mild steel sample, Spheroidisation of high carbon steel, Quenching: study of quenching media, and time effects on hardening of steel, Tempering: Study of tempering temperature and time on tempering of steel, Carburisation of steel and case depth measurement, Heat treatment of Cast iron and stainless steel.

Hum 3127.title: Government and Sociology
topics: Introduction of Government and Politics: Definition of government and politics; Scope and utility of government and politics; Origin and development of the state functions of modern welfare state; Role and quality of ideal citizen. Forms of Government: Definition and forms of government; Distinction between different forms of government.
Democratic Theories: Classical liberalism; Conservatism; Socialism; Contemporary liberalism; Fascism, Marxism, Communism; Nationalism; Democracy in the United States, European Union, Africa and Asia.
Basic Structures of Bangladesh Government: The executive, Legislative and judiciary; Constitution of Bangladesh; Basic principles and theory of governance in Bangladeshi Political system.

Introduction of Sociology: Definition, nature and scope of sociology; Socio-cultural context of the emergence of sociology; Sociological perspective-Functionalism, Conflict perspective and Symbolic interactionism, Sociological imagination.
Basic Concepts of Sociology: Society, Community, Institution, Association, Organization, Group, Kinship, Social Structure, Social stratification.
Methods and Techniques of Research in Sociology: Scientific method, Steps of scientific research; Methods and techniques of sociological research; Ethics of Research.

Culture and Socialization: Definition and elements of culture; Basic concepts of culture-Cultural lag, Cultural relativism, Cultural hybridization, Ethnocentrism, Counter culture, Cultural shock; Definition and agencies of socialization; Theories of socialization; Impact of culture on socialization and personality development.

Social Changes and Social Problems: Definition and agencies of social changes; Industrialization, Urbanization and Social pathology) Crime and Deviance; Globalization and changing pattern of family and marriage; Sociological conceptualization of religion and role of religion in society.

MSE 3201.title: Materials Characterization
topics: Structural Characterization: Crystallography basics; Properties of X-Ray; Diffraction pattern analysis; Phase identification, Phase quantification, Application of X-ray diffraction for phase diagram determination; Construction and operation of Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM)- Crystal structure and Crystal defects detection; Polymeric materials analysis by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman Spectroscopy.

Electrical Characterization: Bulk resistivity and measurement techniques; Spreading resistance technique; Contact resistivity and measurement techniques; Hall effect; Hall scattering factor; Deep-level defect analysis through Deep-level transient spectroscopy (DLTS); Scanning capacitance microscopy (SCM); tunneling-AFM (TUNA) tools for electrical characterization.

Surface Characterization: Basic principle of optical microscopy, Construction, modes of operation and application of Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Specimen preparation for SEM; Operation modes, Image artifacts of atomic force microscope (AFM); Surface profilometer technique.

Compositional Characterization: Fundamental analysis, Qualitative and Quantitative analysis of X-ray emission spectroscopy- Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS), Wavelength Dispersive Spectroscopy (WDS); Basics of electron probe microscopic analysis (EPMA) and Atomic probe microscopy (APM) techniques for compositional analysis; X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS): Auger electron Spectroscopy (AES); Mass Spectroscopy (MS)-different ionization techniques for mass spectroscopy, ICP-MS, LA-MS; Optical Emission Spectroscopy (OES)- Spark-OES, ICP-OES; UV spectroscopy technique.
Thermal Characterization: Common characteristics of thermal events, Differential thermal analysis (DTA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), Thermo gravimetric analysis (TGA).

MSE 3202.title: Materials Characterization Sessional
topics: Experiments based on the topics covered in MSE 3201 course.

MSE 3203.title: Ceramics and Glass Engineering
topics: Structure and Defects of Ceramics: Ceramic bonding and crystal structure; Pauling's rules; Complex ceramic structures; Defects in ceramics; Kröger-Vink notation; Equations for point defects; Dislocations in ceramics; Surfaces and interfaces; Phase boundaries and pores.

Behavior of Ceramics: Mechanical behavior- Strength, Impact properties, Fatigue of ceramics; Fracture behavior; Toughening mechanisms in ceramics; Thermal behavior- Heat capacity, Thermal conductivity, Thermal expansion; Creep and Thermal stresses; Electrical behavior- Electronic conductivity, Ionic conductivity, Electrical insulators, Semiconductors, Superconductivity; Dielectric and magnetic behavior- Polarization, Dielectric properties, Piezoelectricity, Pyroelectricity, Ferroelectricity; Source of magnetism; Magnetic terminology; Applications of magnetic ceramics.

Processing of Ceramics: Powder processing; Shape-forming processes: Pressing, casting, and Plastic forming; Densification: Sintering, Hot pressing, and Hot isostatic pressing; Sol-gel processing; Glazing and decoration of ceramics.

Properties and Processing of Glass: Raw materials of glass making; Composition-and properties of common types of glass; Defects in glass; Glass processing: Processing bulk glass, Bubbles, Flat glass, Float-glass, Glassblowing, Coating glass, Safety glass, Chemical toughening process, Ceramming.

MSE 3204.title: Ceramics and Glass Engineering Sessional
topics: Experiments based on the topics covered in MSE 3203 course.

MSE 3205.title: Corrosion and Surface Engineering
topics: Corrosion
Introduction: Basic concepts; Faraday's law; Corrosion rate expression; Factors affecting corrosion rate; Phenomenological aspects of corrosive attacks.

Fundamentals of Corrosion Reactions: Standard free energy of reaction; Activity of electrolytes; Electrochemical equilibrium; Equilibrium potential and corrosion behavior; Pourbaix diagrams; Passivity; Polarization.
Environmental, Metallurgical and other Effects: Effect of oxygen and oxidizers; Effect of velocity; Effect of temperature; Effect of corrosive concentration; Effect of galvanic coupling.
Different Forms of Corrosion: Galvanic corrosion; Crevice corrosion; Pitting; Intergranular corrosion; Selective leaching; Erosion corrosion; Stress corrosion; Hydrogen damage.
High Temperature Corrosion: Mechanism and kinetics; High temperature materials; Metal-gas reaction at high temperature.
Surface Engineering
Introduction to Surface Engineering: Surface characteristics; Surface and interface; Texture and preparation methods.

Surface Coatings Techniques: Electro-and electroless-plating mechanisms, Bath characteristics and electrochemical parameters; Conversion coatings; Spray coating processes; Hot dipping; Advanced surface coating methods-PVD, CVD and LASER surface modification.

Testing and Quality Control of Coatings: Selection of coating materials and methods; Basic types of wear: Abrasive, Adhesive and Delamination wear; Frictional processes and friction coefficient; Influence of materials properties on wear resistance; Wear tests; Wear resistant materials and coatings.

MSE 3206.title: Corrosion and Surface Engineering Sessional
topics: Experiments based on the MSE 3205 course.

MSE 3208.title: Materials Processing Plant Design Sessional
topics: This laboratory course will help the students understand about the design, erection, operation and maintenance of a materials processing plant and design a product manufacturing plant according to the engineering, economical and environmental consideration.

IEM 3227.title: Industrial Management
topics: Introduction: Evolution and various thoughts of management, Organization and environment. Organization: Theory and structure, Co-ordination, Span of control, Authority, Delegation, Centralization and decentralization.
Personal Management: Need hierarchy, Motivation, Leadership, Method study, Appraisal, Wages and incentives, Organizational change and conflicts.
Cost and Financial Management: Elements of costs of products depreciation, Break even analysis.

Operations Management: Forecasting; Inventory management; Materials requisition planning (MRP); JIT; Master planning basic scheduling technique; CPM and PERT; Plant location and layout; Maintenance management; Manage information system (MIS); Computer aided process planning (CAPP); Manufacturing resource planning (MRP-II).

optionalCourses.title: Materials Recycling and Environmental Aspects
topics: Material Dependence and Resource Consumption: Brief history of materials uses; The reliance on non-renewable materials; Materials use and the environment impact; Resource consumption and reserves; The resource base and resource life.

Environmental Legislation and Economic Factor: International treaties, protocols and conventions; National legislation: Standards, Directives, Taxes, trading tools; Economic instruments: Green taxes and Trading schemes; The consequence of legislation on industry.

The Materials Life Cycle: Life cycle assessment (LCA): Details and difficulties; streamlined LCA; Strategy for eco-selection of materials; Determinants of product life; End of first life; Problem of packaging; Resurrecting the materials: Recycling; Effluent treatment plant (ETP) and Sewage treatment plant (STP) process.
Eco-audit: Eco-attributes of materials; Carbon footprint; Eco-audits system and tools; Case study.

Selection Strategies and Materials for Green Energy: Materials profiles; Familiarize with Metals, Alloys, Polymers, Ceramics and Hybrids composite; Principles of materials selection; Selection criteria and property charts; Computer-aided selection; Case study.
Use of Sustainable Materials and Design for Sustainability: The concept of sustainable development; Ecological metaphor; Sustainable energy; Sustainable materials; Materials value and future options.

optionalCourses.title: Extractive Metallurgy
topics: Ore Processing: Definition of ore, Purposes of ore dressing, Ore handling, Ore sampling, Particle size analysis techniques, Comminution, Crushing techniques, Grinding processes, Industrial screening techniques, Classification and types of classifiers, Gravity separation, Dense medium separation (DMS), Froth flotation, Magnetic and electrical separation, Dewatering, Tailings disposal.

Extractive Metallurgy: Thermodynamic and kinetic principles of metal extraction, Ellingham diagrams. Pyrometallurgical process: Drying, Calcination, Roasting, Smelting. Hydrometallurgical Processes: Leaching, Theory of leaching, Role of oxygen in leaching operations, Bacterial leaching, Selective precipitation, Ion exchange, Solvent extraction, Pyro vs. hydrometallurgy. Electrometallurgical process: Electrolysis, Electrolytic extraction from aqueous and fused salt bath, Electroplating, Cell design.

Extraction of Common Metals: Fe and Sn extraction from consecutive oxides, Electrolytic reduction method of extracting Al and Mg from consecutive oxides, Self-reduction of Pb and Cu from their sulphides, Extraction of precious metals such as: Au, Ag, Pt, and U.

MSE 4101.title: Modern Iron and Steel Making
topics: Iron Making

Blast Furnace Iron Making: Blast furnace-burden preparation; Auxiliary equipment: gas cleaning device, air preheating device; Blast furnace charging sequence; Blast furnace mass and heat balance; Blast furnace reactions; Blast furnace temperature, pressure and composition profile; Operational irregularities and remedial measures in Blast furnaces; Modern trends in Blast Furnace Technology.

Alternative Techniques of Iron Making: Low shaft and charcoal furnaces; Electro-thermal processes; Rotary and Cupola furnace; Sponge iron production; Kinetics of iron oxide reduction; Evaluation of activation energy for various reactions.
Ferroalloy Production: Production of Ferrosilicon; Ferromanganese; Silicomanganese; Ferrochromium; Ferromolybdenum.
Steel Making

Primary Steel Making: History of steel making; Principles of steel making; Raw materials and various steelmaking process: Open hearth furnace, Basic oxygen steelmaking; Induction furnace steelmaking, Electric arc furnace steelmaking; Stainless steel making; Sources of slag and role of slag.
Secondary Steelmaking and Casting: Ladle refining furnace, De-oxidation (or, "killing"), Vacuum degassing, Alloy addition, Inclusion removal, Ingot casting and Continuous casting; Casting defects.

MSE 4103.title: Engineering Alloys and Materials Selection
topics: Engineering Alloys

Ferrous Materials: Different types of ferrous materials:- Plain carbon steels; Low alloy steels; High alloy steels; Stainless steels and maraging steels; Tool steels; High speed steel; Die steels; High strength low alloy steel and study their structure properties relationship and applications.

Nonferrous Materials: Different types of nonferrous materials:- Copper and its alloys; Aluminum and its alloys; Zinc and its alloys; Magnesium and its alloys; Titanium and its alloys; Nickel and its alloys; Magnetic alloys, Super alloys and study their structure properties relationship and applications.
Materials Selection

The Design Process and Material Property Charts: The design process; Types of design; Design tools and materials data; Exploring materials properties; The material property charts; Further understanding and interpretation of materials properties charts; Evolution of structural materials; Holes in material property space.

Basics of Materials Selection: The selection strategy; Material indices; The selection procedure; The structural index; Selection with multiple constraints; Conflicting objectives; Shape factors; Limits to shape efficiency; Material indices including shape; Case studies.

Designing Hybrid Materials and Process Selection: Holes in material-property space; The method: "A+B+C configuration + Scale"; Composites and sandwich structures; Cellular structures foams and lattices; Classifying processes; Systematic process selection; Ranking: Process cost; Case studies.

MSE 4104.title: Engineering Alloys and Materials Selection Sessional
topics: Laboratory based on MSE 4103 by using Cambridge Engineering Selector (CES) EduPack software.

MSE 4105.title: Polymer and Composite Materials
topics: Polymer
Introduction of Polymer: Definition; Classification; Structure and characteristics of different types of polymers; Applications of polymers.

Synthesis and Fabrication: Additional polymerization; Condensation polymerization; Copolymerization; Degree of polymerization; Mechanism of polymerization (free radical, cationic and anionic), Polymer additives and compounding; Processing methods: casting, open mold and close mold, extrusion, injection molding, blow molding, rotational molding, compression molding, calendaring, thermoforming.

Properties of Polymers: Physical and mechanical (hardness, toughness, tensile strength, compression strength, creep, fatigue) properties of polymers, Relation between melting temperature and glass transition temperature properties involving large and small deformation, Property requirements and polymer utilization.
Special Types of Polymers: Polyelectrolytes; Conducting polymers; Biomedical polymers; Thermally stable polymers; Thermoplastic; Liquid crystal polymer, Polymer composites.
Composite

Concept of Composites: Introduction; Types of composite materials, Matrix materials, Reinforcements; Types of fibers; Laminar composites; Flake composites; Filled composites; Particulate reinforced composites; applications of composite.
Fabrication of Composite Materials: Metal matrix composites (MMC); Ceramic matrix composites (CMC); Polymer matrix composites (PMC).

Properties of Composite Materials: Elastic properties of unidirectional and random fiber composites; Hybrid composites; Angle-plied composites; Mechanics of composites; Bonding mechanism adsorption and wetting, Interdiffusion, Mechanical keying, Bond strength coupling agents.

MSE 4106.title: Polymer and Composite Materials Sessional
topics: Experiment based on the topics covered in MSE 4105 course.

MSE 4107.title: Computational Materials Science
topics: Materials Modelling and Simulation: Computational materials science, Methods in computational materials science, Basic procedures of computational materials science, Monte Carlo method, Molecular dynamics, The random-walk model, Simulation to finite system.

Molecular Dynamics: Basics of molecular dynamics for atomic systems, Velocity rescaling, Molecular dynamics in other ensembles, Accelerated dynamics, Limitation of molecular dynamics, Molecular dynamics in materials research, Potentials, Solutions for Newton's equations of motion, Initialization, Integration /equilibration, Data production.

Mesoscopic Methods: Kinetic Monte Carlo method, Monte Carlo methods at the mesoscale, Cellular automata, Phase field methods: Conserved and non-conserved order parameters, Governing equations, One dimensional phase field calculation, Free energy of an interface, Local free energy functions, Other applications in materials research.

Density Functional Theory: Introduction, Kohn-Sham approach, Kohn-Sham equations, Exchange-correlation functional, Solving Kohn-Sham equations, DFT extensions and limitations, DFT exercises with quantum espresso: Quantum espresso, Si2-convergence test, Si2-band, Si7-vacancy, Si7-vacancy diffusion.

MSE 4108.title: Computational Materials Science Sessional
topics: Sessional based on the topics covered in MSE 4107 course.

MSE 4109.title: Electronic, Magnetic and Optical Properties of Materials
topics: Electronic Properties: Electronic and ionic conduction, Colliding and drifting electrons, Electron in a potential well (bound electron), Finite potential barrier (tunnel effect), Electron in a periodic field of a crystal (the solid state), Band structure for metals and semiconductors, Fermi energy and Fermi surface, Complete density of states function within a band, Conduction in terms of band and atomic bonding models, Band gap engineering, Carrier transport phenomena, Hall effect, Mobility and carrier density in metals and nonmetals, Capacitance, Polarization of dielectrics, Dielectric constant, Current distribution, DC insulator and AC conductor (skin effect).

Magnetic Properties: Magnetic dipole, Origin of magnetic moment, Magnetization in a spin, Diamagnetism and paramagnetism, Ferromagnetism, Antiferromagnetism and ferrimagnetism, Langevin equation for dia & para magnetism, Curie law, Theory of paramagnetism, The influence of temperature on magnetic behavior, Domains and hysteresis, Magnetic anisotropy, Soft magnetic materials, Hard magnetic materials, Magnetic storage, Effect of magnetic properties on superconductivity.

Optical Properties: Optical constants: index of refraction, damping constant, reflectivity, and transmittance; Hagen-Rubens relation, Electromagnetic radiation. Atomistic theory of the optical properties: Free electrons without damping, Free electrons with damping (classical free electron theory of metals), Reflectivity, Bound electrons (classical electron theory of dielectric materials), Contributions of free electrons and harmonic oscillators to the optical constants. Absorption of light by interband and intraband transitions, Optical spectra of materials, Dispersion, Photoconductivity.

MSE 4201.title: Materials for Energy Conversion and Storage
topics: Energy conversion
Solar Cells: Photovoltaics; Inorganic, organic and perovskite solar cells.

Fuel Cells: Characteristics of fuel cell, Alkaline, Proton exchange membrane, Polymer electrolyte membrane, Direct methanol, Phosphoric acid, and Molten carbonate fuel cells, Solid oxide electrolytes.
Nuclear Fusion: Muon catalysed fusion, Pyroelectric fusion, Condensation fusion in solids, Fusion reactor materials; Fusion wastes.
Nuclear Fission: Nuclear fuel supply- uranium and plutonium, Thorium, Core components-nuclear fuels, Cladding materials, Out-of-core materials; Fission wastes.
Energy Storage

Hydrogen Storage: Metal oxide framework (MOF), Organic frameworks, Simple and complex hydrides, Carbonaceous materials-graphite, graphene, carbon nanotube, fullerenes, carbon nitride, Boron nitride nanomaterials, Zeolites and glass microspheres, Storage in polymers.
Batteries: Lead-acid battery, Na-S battery, Ni-Cd battery, Ni-MH battery, Li-ion battery, Metal-air batteries- Zinc-air, Li-air, Na-air.

Electrochemical Capacitors: Supercapacitors-electrodes, electrolytes, 2D materials, Flexible supercapacitors, Pseudocapacitors-metal oxide electrodes, Polymer electrodes, Li-ion capacitors. Piezoelectric energy harvesting and storage, Hybrid materials for energy conversion and storage.

MSE 4202.title: Materials for Energy Conversion and Storage Sessional
topics: Experiment based on the topics covered in MSE 4201.

MSE 4211.title: Professional Ethics
topics: Ethics vs. engineering ethics, Engineering and professionalism, Psychological basis of ethics, Religion and ethics, Egoism and relativism, Utilitarianism and rational utilitarianism, Ethics and other branches of knowledge, Intuitionism.

Concept of moral thoughts and moral judgment, Bases of human behavior, Moral development and reasoning, Morality and social institution, Moral rights and duties, Interpersonal moral sentiment, Occupational culture and ideology, Occupational stress, Morality and religion, Organizational commitment, Morality in international context.

Professionalism and codes of ethics, Engineering as social experimentation, Institutional ethics, Academic ethics, Understanding ethical problems, Ethical problems solving techniques, Professional responsibilities, Professional rights, Environmental ethics, Computer ethics, Analyzing issues of ethical problems, Utilitarian thinking respect for persons.

MSE 4214.title: Failure Analysis Sessional
topics: Failure Analysis of Engineering Components:
Case Histories

Inspection of the failure of different engineering samples/components based on microscopic examination, chemical analysis, mechanical properties examination, nondestructive examination, analysis of data.
Artifact Investigation:
Dismantling and identification of materials of engineering components for improvement of engineering products.

MSE 4216.title: Technical Seminar
topics: Theories and practical examples on real case studies to help the students develop the ability to gain knowledge on the rapid advancements in the field of Materials Science via self-learning techniques; Preparation of models, charts and reports based on the knowledge acquired from the studies and pointing out the salient features; Development of cognitive ability; Enhancement in communication, interpersonal skills, openness to criticism, improvement based on feedback; Recognizing the importance of voice and visual aids to enhance the presentation skill; Acknowledging students with the appropriate mannerism to present papers, official or, academic proposals, thesis etc.

EEE 4227.title: Semiconductor Materials and Devices
topics: Semiconductor Materials and Properties: Introduction, Intrinsic semiconductor, Extrinsic semiconductor, Drift and diffusion Current, Excess carrier.

PN Junctions and Diodes: Basic structure of the p-n junction, Zero applied bias, Reverse applied bias, Junction breakdown, Diode circuit models, Current-Voltage relationship, Other types of diodes: Zener diode, etc. Diode applications.

The Bipolar Transistor: The bipolar transistor action, Minority carrier distribution, Transistor current components, Different transistor configurations, Transistor as a switch and amplifier, Transistor biasing, Thermal stabilization.
The Junction Field-Effect Transistor: JFET concepts, The device characteristics, FET amplifier.
Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor: The two-terminal MOS structure, The basic MOSFET operation, MOSFET types, MOSFET as a switch and amplifier.
Metal-Semiconductor and Hetero-Junctions: The schottky barrier diode, Metal-semiconductor ohmic contacts, Heterojunctions.
Optical Devices: Optical absorption, Photodetectors, Photoluminescence and electroluminescence, Light emitting diodes, Laser diodes.
Semiconductor Power Devices: Tunnel diode, Gunn diode, Impatt diode, Power bipolar transistors, Power MOSFETs, The thyristor, DIAC, TRIAC.

Hum 4227.title: Project Management and Entrepreneurship
topics: Project Management Basics: Definition, Types and characteristics of projects, Triple constraints of project management, Project methodologies, Parts of a standard project, Projects vs. programs vs. portfolios, Project stakeholders.
Project Conceptualizing and Initiating: Developing success criteria, Creating the business case, Cost benefit analysis, Developing the project charter.

Project Planning: The work breakdown structure, Specification, Estimating using effort and duration, Techniques for accurate estimates, Methods to calculate start and finish dates of tasks, Network diagrams, Critical path method, Resource planning, Creating a project milestone schedule, Performance indicator, Project management tools, Gantt charts, Identifying and quantifying project risks, SWOT analysis, Financial management, Budget, Procurement, Procurement management, Case studies.

Project Execution and Control: Creating a high-performing project team, Team training, Techniques for effective communication and status reporting, Earned value management (EVM), Project scope management and developing a change control plan, Monitoring, Evaluation and managing risks and issues, Managing stakeholder expectations.
Project Closing: Scope verification, Transferring deliverables to the customer, Suitability of project and issues, Post-project review or evaluation.

Entrepreneurship: Theories of entrepreneurship, Types of entrepreneurship ventures, Roles of an entrepreneur, Innovation, Entrepreneurship process, Problem identification, Idea vs. opportunity, Business models and business planning, Financial statements.

optionalCourses.title: Biomaterials
topics: Fundamentals of Biomaterials: The necessity of biomaterials; Properties and sources of biomaterials; Natural biomaterials and biomimetic materials, Fundamentals of cell biology and biological systems, Biocompatibility, Cell-biomaterial interactions.

Biomaterial Alloys: Structure and properties of nitinol, Ferrous shape memory alloys (SMA), Stainless steel alloys, Copper based SMA, Cobalt-chromium based alloys, Titanium alloys; Tantalum and magnesium alloys in biomedical applications.

Bio-polymers and Bio-composites: Properties and applications of polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA), polylactic acids (PLA), polyglycolic acids (PGA), polycaprolactone (PCL) and polyurethanes biopolymers; Biodegradability in polymers; Colloids for biomedical applications; Hydrogels, Electroresponsive shape memory effect in bio-polymers; Biomedical composites; Composites as orthopedic implants.

Bio-ceramics: Bioactive glass, alumina, zirconia, calcium phosphates (CaP), hydroxyapatites (HA), tricalcium phosphates (TCP) bioceramics; Shape memory effect in ceramics and corresponding application. Advances in pyrolytic and activated carbon as biomaterials; Surface modification of biomedical implants, Drug delivery.

optionalCourses.title: Materials in Extreme Environments
topics: Materials Under High Pressure: Experimental and theoretical methods involved in the study of materials under pressure, Pressure induced phase transitions, Amorphization, Negative thermal expansion, Recrystallization of amorphous phase and dissociation in materials.

Materials Under Extreme Temperature: Intermetallics; Nickel, titanium, iron and zirconium aluminides, silicides, high entropy alloys and superalloys under high temperature environment; Glass-ceramics and their properties; Glass-ceramic sealants used for high temperature applications; Machinable glass-ceramics; Properties of refractories; Thermal expansion of materials; Correlation of physical properties with thermal expansion; Laser-induced vaporization-mass spectrometry on refractories under ultrahigh temperature. Thermal, mechanical and electrical properties of materials in cryogenic temperatures.

Materials Under High Stress Condition: Dynamic compression process; Mechanical properties of Al alloys in high strain rate; Shock wave induced omega phase transformation in zirconium and zirconium-niobium alloys; Study of phase transitions in uranium and thorium carbides; Severe plastic deformation of materials; Stress-grain size relation; Strain rate sensitivity; Fatigue and superelasticity under severe plastic deformation.

Materials in Hostile Chemical Environments: Reactions between slag and refractories; Pozzolans, tungsten and silicon carbides, boron and gallium nitrides, borosilicate glass and diamond based corrosion resistant materials; Resins, polymers and composites under harsh chemical environment; Chlorine and fluorinated polymers; Corrosion of polyethylene terephthalate (PET); Materials for the construction of pickling and galvanizing tanks.

optionalCourses.title: Nano-structured Materials
topics: Nanomaterials: Homogeneous nucleation of nanoparticles; Growth of nuclei; Spontaneous growth of nanowires and nanorods; Two dimensional nanomaterial thin films; Three dimensional superlattices; Superclusters and colloidal crystals; Carbon fullerenes; Nanotubes; Micro and mesoporous materials; Metal-metal, metal-oxide, semiconductor-oxide and oxide-oxide type core-shell structures; Organic-inorganic hybrids; Intercalation compounds; Nanocomposites and nanograined materials; Properties of nanocrystals; Importance of nanostructured materials; Challenges in nanotechnology.

Fabrication of Nanomaterials: Synthesis of metallic, semiconductor and oxide nanoparticles through heterogeneous nucleation; Kinetically confined synthesis of nanoparticles; Template based synthesis of nanowires and nanorods; Fabrication of thin film form and their interaction with the substrates, Electric arc deposition, Molecular beam epitaxy, Growth mechanisms, Epitaxial and kinetic effects in thin films, Synthesis of metal and semiconductor nanoparticles through colloidal routes; Sol-gel method of synthesis of nanoparticles and thin films, Hydrothermal synthesis, Sonochemical synthesis, Microwave synthesis, Nanolithography, Different methods of microfabrication,

Applications: Nanoelectronics; Nanodots; Biological applications of nanoparticles; Catalysis by gold nanoparticles; Band gap engineered quantum devices; Nanomechanics; Carbon nanotube emitters; Photo electrochemical cells; Photonic crystals and plasmon waveguides; Automobiles; Sports and toys; Textiles; Medical field; Agriculture and food; Space; Defence and engineering.

optionalCourses.title: Materials and Sustainable Development
topics: Materials, Energy and Sustainability: Environmental, social and economical aspects of materials usage and development; Sustainability; Sustainable development; Articulations of sustainable development.
Assessing Sustainable Developments: Dealing with complex systems; A layered approach to assessing a sustainable development; Assembling the layer; The detailed 5 steps.

Materials Supply-Chain Risk: Emerging constraint on material sourcing and usage; Price volatility risk; Monopoly of supply and geopolitical risk; Conflict risk; Legislation and regulation risk; Abundance risk; Changing expectation of corporate responsibility; Managing risk.
Corporate Sustainability and Materials: Corporate social responsibility and sustainability reporting; Case studies: Corporate SRs.

Case Studies: The structure of the case studies; Articulations of sustainable development that went wrong; Biopolymers to replace oil-based plastics; Wind farms as a source of renewable energy; Electric cars as the future for clean personal transport; Lighting incandescent, fluorescent, LED; Solar PV for low-carbon power; Bamboo as a sustainable building material.
Circular Materials Economy: The ecological metaphor; The scale of the vision; The circular materials economy, Creating a circular materials economy.
